status_summary: HUD has reviewed and withdrawn guidance under Executive Orders 14192 and 14219, and its Office of General Counsel notice of 2026-07-17 states that HUD is undertaking a comprehensive review of its subregulatory guidance. An Office of Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity memo of 2025-09-17 withdrew nine documents, formalized in a notice published 2026-04-06 (91 FR 17291, eight documents, effective 2025-09-17), and the Office of General Counsel notice (91 FR 44867) withdrew 13 documents effective 2025-09-25, covering topics such as criminal records screening, source of income, limited English proficiency, special purpose credit and appraisal elements of proof. HUD said it withdrew guidance that was not statutorily required, was inconsistent with the governing statute or regulation, or added compliance burdens. The HUD Secretary said on 2025-02-28 that the department was taking inventory of burdensome regulations.

timeline.event: The HUD Secretary said at a builders' conference that HUD was taking inventory of and terminating burdensome regulations.

HUD's Office of Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity, in a memo signed by its Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary citing Executive Orders 14192 and 14219, withdrew nine fair housing guidance documents (including items on limited English proficiency, assistance animals, criminal records, source of income and digital advertising), each found to fail at least one of three criteria; the memo says the withdrawals are not necessarily final.

title: Review and withdraw HUD subregulatory guidance issued outside notice and comment
uncertainties: Both notices carry effective dates in September 2025, earlier than publication, because they formalize withdrawals made earlier. Both were read in full on federalregister.gov in review: the July 2026 notice (91 FR 44867) states that HUD is undertaking a comprehensive review of its sub-regulatory guidance, and the April 2026 notice (91 FR 17291) applies a three-part test (statutorily prescribed, consistent with statute or regulation, reduces compliance burdens) and says FHEO is still reviewing its guidance. A Federal Register API query of HUD documents since 2026-04-01, run in review on 2026-10-18, found only these two guidance withdrawal notices; no rounds from single family, public housing or community development offices were documented, and no inventory of reviewed guidance has been published. The memo of 2025-09-17 was read as a copy hosted by animallaw.info (an academic animal-law center), not on hud.gov; it lists nine documents against eight in the April 2026 notice, and the two overlap almost entirely.
